(This evening through Sunday)...
Issued at 255 PM EDT Sun Aug 9 2026

Bottom line up front...Repeated rounds of thunderstorms are expected 
this week. Severe storms are possible into Tuesday, and heavy rain 
and resultant flooding are possible at least into mid-week.

Rest of This Afternoon into Early Evening...

Generally quiet weather is expected for this period, with 
very warm to hot and humid conditions. 

Weakening convection across central Illinois at the moment should 
diminish in coverage to less than mentionable by the time it reaches 
the forecast area. However, will continue to monitor for the need to 
add an isolated shower mention to portions of the southern two-
thirds of the area.

Across the northern third or so, additional convection may develop 
to the south of the current area from northern Illinois into lower 
Michigan. Have put slight chance PoPs in to cover this threat. A 
strong storm with gusty winds cannot be ruled out given the 
instability, but shear is weak enough that odds for severe look low.

Mid evening into Monday morning...

Focus then turns to the develop of an MCS. An 850mb jet should 
initiate convection to the northwest of central Indiana, most likely 
near the old outflow from this afternoon's convection. The MCS will 
then turn southeast as the 850mb flow veers during the night. 

Unfortunately, high uncertainty remains on exactly where this will 
occur. Given the setup, would believe that the highest chances for 
rain will be north and east of the forecast area. However, as CAMs 
show in their forecasts, many solutions are possible. For now, will 
go high end chance PoPs northeast overnight with lower PoPs 
elsewhere. As the MCS weakens Monday morning, will have chance PoPs 
east and lower PoPs west.

With increasing shear and continued good instability, severe storms 
are possible. Damaging winds will be the primary threat. Heavy rain 
and resultant localized flooding will also be possible with 
efficient rainfall processes. 

Monday afternoon and night...

Higher uncertainty will exist in this period as some convective 
development will depend on how tonight's convection evolves, and 
then the next round will depend on the previous round.

Some upper energy may kick off another complex of storms Monday 
afternoon, again mainly northeast. Will go with chance PoPs there 
and lower PoPs elsewhere. Monday night, similar conditions to 
tonight will ignite another MCS which could move through the area 
overnight Monday night. This one could be more into the forecast 
area, so went likely PoPs northeast and lower PoPs elsewhere.

With high instability and decent shear, severe storms will once 
again be possible. Damaging winds will be the primary threat, but 
large hail and an isolated tornado cannot be ruled out. Heavy rain 
will continue to be a threat, and will have to closely watch for 
heavy rain moving over the same areas multiple times.

Looking at temperatures, if clouds from the morning MCS don't stick 
around, highs in the upper 80s to lower 90s will occur Monday. With 
the high dewpoints, heat indices around 100 are possible, especially 
south.

Tuesday and Wednesday...

Central Indiana will remain in northwest flow aloft, and a surface 
front will remain in the area. This will keep the stage set for 
clusters of showers and thunderstorms to move through. Locally heavy 
rain will remain a threat and will have the potential for falling 
over the same locations. Instability and shear will combine to keep 
the possibility of severe storms around, especially Tuesday. 
Damaging winds look to be the primary severe threat.

However, as is the case with previous days, the devil is in the 
details. Uncertainty remains on the timing of the thunderstorm 
clusters as well as how each around will affect the others (in terms 
of cloud cover impacting instability, leftover boundaries, etc). 
These will also impact which areas see the best chances for 
convection as well.

Will have likely PoPs at times through this period. Initially 
focusing on the northern forecast area, these will gradually shift 
south into Wednesday night as the surface boundary gradually does 
the same. Confidence in the specific timing remains low.

Heat will remain a potential threat, mainly Tuesday across the 
south (the south has initially the lower chances for rain and cloud 
cover). Heat indices may reach around 100 degrees if rain/clouds 
hold off. Wednesday's readings may be a few degrees cooler with the 
increased clouds/rain chances.

Thursday onward...

The surface front will continue to move slowly south, eventually 
getting south of the forecast area by the weekend. This will allow 
cooler air to filter in, with highs in the upper 70s to middle 80s 
Friday into the weekend.
